about: The reviewed dependencies, checked by scripts/dependency-policy.ts. The rules and how to add, bump or remove a dependency: docs/security/dependency-policy.md. Edit direct, installScripts and submodules by hand; refresh resolved with node scripts/dependency-policy.ts --write.

@anthropic-ai/sdk.why: The App's calls to Claude for triage and Bounty review, with structured output parsed through zod. The model only advises; nothing pays out on its answer.
@anthropic-ai/sdk.exit: Call the Messages API with fetch and validate the JSON with zod: about 100 lines, losing the SDK's retries and typed errors.

@octokit/auth-app.why: Signs the GitHub App's JWT with its private key and exchanges it for installation tokens, which every call the App makes to GitHub needs.
@octokit/auth-app.exit: Sign the RS256 JWT with node:crypto and cache installation tokens ourselves: small, but it is the App's credential handling, so we'd rather run the reviewed library.

@octokit/rest.why: The App's GitHub REST client: checks, comments, labels, pull requests and issues, with pagination and retries.
@octokit/rest.exit: fetch against api.github.com for the dozen endpoints the App uses, with our own pagination.

@modelcontextprotocol/server.why: The MCP server protocol and its stdio transport, which let an AI agent call the agent package's tools to read a repo's rules and make a Deposit.
@modelcontextprotocol/server.exit: None short of writing the MCP protocol ourselves; it is the reference implementation.

@modelcontextprotocol/client.why: The agent package's tests drive its MCP server through a real client, over stdio and HTTP, as an AI agent would.

viem.why: Everything on Arc: ABI encoding, EIP-712 and EIP-3009 typed data, signature checks, RPC calls and the Keeper's transactions. The sdk declares it as a peer and builds against it; the App, the agent and the pages ship it.
viem.exit: None reasonable: it is the chain library the whole repo is built on.

yaml.why: Parses a repo's .github/bona-fide.yml, in the App and in the setup page's preview. It has no dependencies of its own.
yaml.exit: The config is a few flat keys: a strict hand-written subset parser would do, at the cost of YAML's edge cases.

zod.why: Validates untrusted input at the edges: the MCP tools' arguments in the agent, and the model's structured answers in the App.
zod.exit: Hand-written validators for each shape; the MCP server and the Anthropic SDK's helpers both expect zod schemas, so it would stay as their dependency.

@types/node.why: Node's type declarations for tsc --noEmit; Node strips types at run time, so nothing of it ships.

prettier.why: Formats the TypeScript at 120 columns (npm run format), and the root's eslint.config.ts, so diffs carry only real changes.

typescript.why: tsc --noEmit type-checks every workspace; Node runs the sources directly, so the compiler never emits code that ships.

vitest.why: The test runner for every workspace, including the anvil and Chrome suites.

rolldown.why: Bundles the pages in web/build.ts so they load nothing from another site, and the App's portability test bundles its source the same way.
rolldown.exit: esbuild would do the same job; rolldown was chosen for its plugin API. Either is a build-time tool only.

eslint.why: npm run lint: one flat config at the root lints every package's sources, tests and build scripts, and fails on any finding. It finds bugs; Prettier formats.
eslint.exit: Rely on tsc --noEmit and code review alone, losing the typed rules (floating promises, unsafe any, exhaustive switches) that tsc doesn't check.

@eslint/js.why: ESLint's recommended JavaScript rules, which eslint.config.ts applies to the landing page's scripts and under typescript-eslint's rules.

typescript-eslint.why: The TypeScript parser and the strictTypeChecked and stylisticTypeChecked rules ESLint runs over every package, reading each package's tsconfig.json through the project service.

@typescript/typescript6.why: TypeScript 6, installed at the root as "typescript": "npm:@typescript/typescript6@6.0.2", for typescript-eslint only. typescript-eslint needs TypeScript's JavaScript API, which TypeScript 7 doesn't have yet, so ESLint loads 6.0.2 while each package keeps typescript 7.0.2 for tsc. Published by the TypeScript team, as Microsoft's 7.0 notes advise for tools that need the API.
@typescript/typescript6.exit: Drop the alias once typescript-eslint supports TypeScript 7's API; the root then needs no TypeScript of its own.

@vitest/eslint-plugin.why: ESLint rules for the vitest suites in every package, such as expects that can't run and focused or skipped tests left in.
@vitest/eslint-plugin.exit: Drop it and lose those rules; vitest itself keeps running the tests.

eslint-config-prettier.why: Turns off every ESLint rule that would argue with Prettier's layout, so Prettier stays the only formatter.
eslint-config-prettier.exit: List the conflicting stylistic rules as off in eslint.config.ts by hand.

globals.why: The browser's global names, which eslint.config.ts declares for the landing page's scripts so no-undef knows window and document.
globals.exit: Declare the few globals the landing page's scripts use in eslint.config.ts by hand.

installScripts.fsevents: macOS only (os: darwin), an optional peer of vite's file watcher. Its install script is `node-gyp rebuild` of the native module it ships prebuilt; it never runs on Linux CI or in the Docker image, which also install with --ignore-scripts. Reviewed 2026-10-19.

contracts/lib/openzeppelin-contracts.why: SafeERC20, ReentrancyGuard, EIP712 and SignatureChecker are compiled into the escrow, the Charity router and the Bounty wallets. The contracts on Arc were built from this tag; moving it changes only the next deployment.

contracts/lib/forge-std.why: Foundry's test and script library: the unit, fuzz and invariant suites and the deploy scripts. Nothing of it is deployed.
